audience.summary: Travellers and hosts choosing where to stay or eat, often on a phone, comparing three or four places on the same evening. They need to trust the room and the welcome before they need the story.

assertions.text: The primary audience is the person making this decision in Cape Coast: someone comparing two or three local options on a phone and looking for evidence that this business can do the job.
Local context matters: check-in, parking, the walk from the station or castle, breakfast and the cancellation terms around Cape Coast should be answered before a visitor is asked to enquire.

positioning.summary: The approved Brand Kit describes this business as calm, warm, understated, hospitable. A quiet colonial-era house at the hour guests arrive: bone plaster, deep green shade, brass and water. Photography is warm and low, never a showroom.

assertions.text: Personality: calm, warm, understated, hospitable.
Tone of voice: Warm, direct and unhurried. Name the room, the view and the price; never oversell the welcome.
Positioning is a design argument, not a claim about the market: the direction should make the business recognisable without inventing an award, a client list or a heritage.

objectives.summary: Check availability or reserve a room directly, with dates, price and cancellation terms visible before the booking form. The site has one primary conversion; everything else supports it.

assertions.text: Primary conversion supported by the current site: book online.

evidence.note: Inferred from the contact or selling route the page publishes.

assertions.text: Measure the direction by qualified enquiries, not by time on page: a completed book online with the information the business needs to reply.
The primary action appears in the first viewport on mobile and again at the end of the story; no competing secondary action may look equally important.

atmosphere.summary: Calm, warm and quietly confident. Arrival, light, linen, a drink offered before the form. Nothing hurried or over-familiar. The atmosphere is a creative proposal, not a description of how the business already feels; it should be tested in review and refined, not asserted in copy.

assertions.text: Proposed emotional register: calm, warm, understated. Every section should hold that register; a playful illustration or a neon gradient would break it.

Avoid the default local-business mood: stock handshakes, generic “Welcome to Adwoa's House”, gold gradients and template testimonials. If the business has no testimonial yet, leave the space empty and say so.

storytelling.summary: The page should read as a sequence, not a list of sections: Arrival and the first impression → The room and how it is made up → The table, the neighbourhood and the day → A reason to return. Each chapter earns the next; no chapter is a grid of unsupported claims.

assertions.text: Proposed narrative arc: Arrival and the first impression; The room and how it is made up; The table, the neighbourhood and the day; A reason to return.
Photography and copy must come from the business. A narrative built on stock images of another place is not this business’s story and will be rejected in review.

artDirection.summary: A quiet colonial-era house at the hour guests arrive: bone plaster, deep green shade, brass and water. Photography is warm and low, never a showroom. The direction below extends that approved visual direction rather than replacing it.

assertions.text: Approved visual direction: A quiet colonial-era house at the hour guests arrive: bone plaster, deep green shade, brass and water. Photography is warm and low, never a showroom.
Materials and texture: plaster, timber, linen, ceramic, water. One material may be exaggerated; all of them may not.
External references are recorded as links and notes only, with a licence status. Nothing is downloaded, traced, recoloured or presented as the Studio’s own.

layout.summary: The direction will compare at least three different composition families — not one layout with three colourways. Each must state its grid, navigation, hero idea and how it collapses at 360px.

assertions.text: Composition is chosen for the business, not for the component library: editorial columns, a cinematic frame, an asymmetric offset, a catalogue index, a quiet centre and a modular block system are all available.
Avoid the default card wall: equal rounded panels with shadows and icons are not a design idea. If a card is used, it must have a reason and a different span.
Every composition is drawn mobile-first at 360px and checked at 768px and 1440px; no essential content may appear only on a wide screen.

typography.summary: Instrument Serif for display and Archivo for text. The modern (high-contrast) serif display face carries the voice while the grotesque sans body face keeps reading effortless. Very high stroke contrast and tight spacing: a headline face, not a text face. Set no smaller than 28px, with generous tracking at small display sizes and no long paragraphs.

assertions.text: Approved Brand Kit type: Display — Instrument Serif (400), SIL Open Font License 1.1.
Licences: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Both permit web embedding and self-hosting. The Studio does not download or redistribute font files without permission.
Language coverage is confirmed for English. If the site will publish Twi, Ewe, Ga or Dagbani, the pairing must change to a family with documented orthography coverage.

colour.summary: Colour is a system with roles, not a collection of swatches: a ground, a surface, ink, secondary ink, one accent and the text that sits on it. Contrast is computed before the palette is proposed.

assertions.text: Approved Brand Kit palette (version 1): Bone #F3EDE2, Ink green #1E241F, Deep palm #31533F, Brass #B98A54.
Contrast checks: 13.58:1, 12.79:1, 4.55:1, 8.12:1, 3.03:1. Text pairs are adjusted until they meet WCAG 2.2 AA; a palette that fails contrast is not a direction.
The accent is used sparingly and for one job: action, emphasis or a single material note. Multiple accents, decorative gradients and coloured cards are rejected in review.

photography.summary: Work from 2 approved files in the vault, art-directed for arrival, light and room detail.

assertions.text: courtyard-evening.jpg (Commissioned photography) — venue photo, approved for private prototype use.
room-linen-detail.jpg (Commissioned photography) — venue photo, approved for private prototype use.
Approved mark: adwoas-house-mark.png (Client-supplied mark). The mark may appear in the prototype; it does not license the site for publication.
Remote images are references, never assets: they are not fetched, cached, displayed inline or offered as “use this image”. A new upload with provenance is the only route into the vault.

motion.summary: One motion idea carries the page: a reveal, a transition or a mask — never all of them at once. Motion clarifies sequence, gives feedback and then gets out of the way.

assertions.text: Every movement has a reduced-motion alternative that removes translation and scroll-linking while leaving the content visible and the focus order intact.
Only opacity, transform and clip-path may be animated; durations stay under 900ms and no motion may delay the first readable frame.
Hover is never the only route to information, and the primary action is never hidden behind an animation.

mobile.summary: The phone is the first canvas, not a compressed desktop. Composition, type and imagery are drawn at 360px before they are expanded.

assertions.text: Body text stays at or above 16px, tap targets at or above 44px, and no horizontal scrolling is permitted at 360px.
The primary action (book online) is reachable in the first viewport and repeated at the end; navigation uses the same labels and order at every width.
Images are cropped for portrait first, with explicit dimensions to prevent layout shift; no full-bleed video is required to understand the page.

accessibility.summary: Accessibility is a constraint on the art direction, not a clean-up task after it. A concept that cannot meet WCAG 2.2 AA is not finished.

assertions.text: WCAG 2.2 AA: text contrast at least 4.5:1, large text and UI at least 3:1, visible focus, logical heading order and labels for every control.
Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion; no content flashes more than three times per second; animation can be paused or is not essential.
The business must supply or approve alt text, captions and transcripts for its own photography, video and audio before publication.

concepts.name: A Quiet Room
concepts.idea: Give one idea per screen enough space to be believed, and let the absence of decoration signal confidence. For Adwoa's House in Cape Coast, that means the work is about arrival, the room, the table and the reason to return.
concepts.narrative: A narrow centred measure, a short statement, one image, then the next thought. The page is shorter than it looks and quieter than the competition. The restraint is the design idea, not the absence of one. The opening line, “A quieter kind of attention.”, is a creative proposal and will be replaced or approved with the business’s own wording before publication.

typography.rationale: Instrument Serif for display and Work Sans for text. The modern (high-contrast) serif display face carries the voice while the grotesque sans body face keeps reading effortless. Very high stroke contrast and tight spacing: a headline face, not a text face. Set no smaller than 28px, with generous tracking at small display sizes and no long paragraphs. The direction keeps the approved Brand Kit face and changes the supporting voice and scale.

concepts.name: First Light
concepts.idea: Design the first ten seconds as an arrival: one place, one horizon, one line of type, and enough quiet for the visitor to want to step inside. For Adwoa's House in Cape Coast, that means the work is about arrival, the room, the table and the reason to return.
concepts.narrative: A full-bleed frame holds the opening. Type enters like a title card and then recedes. The page unfolds in scenes, each one a different hour of the same place, with the practical details arriving only after the atmosphere has earned attention. The opening line, “Arrive slowly.”, is a creative proposal and will be replaced or approved with the business’s own wording before publication.

typography.rationale: Instrument Serif for display and Public Sans for text. The modern (high-contrast) serif display face carries the voice while the grotesque sans body face keeps reading effortless. Very high stroke contrast and tight spacing: a headline face, not a text face. Set no smaller than 28px, with generous tracking at small display sizes and no long paragraphs. The direction keeps the approved Brand Kit face and changes the supporting voice and scale.

typography.notes: Very high stroke contrast and tight spacing: a headline face, not a text face. Set no smaller than 28px, with generous tracking at small display sizes and no long paragraphs. concepts.name: Notes from the House
concepts.idea: Build the page from annotated observations: a running note in the margin, a photograph pinned beside it, and a tone that sounds like someone who was there. For Adwoa's House in Cape Coast, that means the work is about arrival, the room, the table and the reason to return.
concepts.narrative: The page reads as a set of notes from the place: dated observations, material samples, a short interview with the maker. It is informal in structure but exacting in detail, and it gives the business a voice no template can copy. The opening line, “Notes from this week.”, is a creative proposal and will be replaced or approved with the business’s own wording before publication.

typography.rationale: Instrument Serif for display and Source Sans 3 for text. The modern (high-contrast) serif display face carries the voice while the humanist sans body face keeps reading effortless. Very high stroke contrast and tight spacing: a headline face, not a text face. Set no smaller than 28px, with generous tracking at small display sizes and no long paragraphs. The direction keeps the approved Brand Kit face and changes the supporting voice and scale.

Open apertures and a comfortable rhythm at 15–17px. One of the most legible faces on inexpensive Android screens; a sensible body default.

colour.strategy: Oat paper, dark ink, an olive support and the brand accent used like a pencil mark. Photographs are pinned, not framed; annotations are set in a smaller, quieter size.

composition.label: Editorial columns
composition.grid: 12 columns, 24px gutter, margins 20px mobile / 64px desktop, maximum 1320px. Text occupies columns 1–7; captions and metadata live in 8–12. The asymmetry is the composition.
composition.navigation: A single line of text links above a hairline rule; the current page is marked with a short accent underline, not a pill.
composition.hero: A headline set across seven columns, a standfirst in the margin, and one tall photograph that begins below the fold.
composition.spacing: Long vertical pauses between chapters, tight leading inside a chapter. Rules, not shadows, separate ideas.
composition.imageComposition: Portrait and square crops, deliberately unequal; captions in the margin; no rounded corners.

imagery.direction: Photographs as evidence with captions that say when and where: a batch, a delivery, a room before service, a note in a notebook. Slight imperfection is welcome; stock polish is not.
imagery.treatment: Images sit beside the note they belong to, revealed by a hard edge. Mixed portrait and landscape crops with handwritten-feeling captions set in the body face.
missing: Collect a week of honest process photographs with dates, plus one short interview with the person who runs the work.

rationale.audience: Travellers and hosts choosing where to stay or eat, often on a phone, comparing three or four places on the same evening. They need to trust the room and the welcome before they need the story. Notes from the House answers that by specificity is more persuasive than polish.
rationale.business: For Adwoa's House in Cape Coast, the direction puts arrival, the room, the table and the reason to return at the centre rather than treating the website as a container for services. It accepts the trade-offs below in exchange for a specific point of view.

observationLabels: Trading name: Adwoa's House, a nine-room guest house in Cape Coast.
Location: A short walk from the castle, on a quiet street with a walled garden.
Contact routes published: The homepage publishes a booking enquiry form and a WhatsApp link.
Primary conversion supported by the current site: book online.
notes: Brand Kit version 1, approved by a named reviewer.
The concept is a creative proposal, not a claim about the business.

tradeoffs: Requires ongoing content, not a one-off build
Informality can undercut a premium price
Harder to keep tidy at scale
The approved Brand Kit face is fixed; variation comes from the supporting face and the scale.
Cannot be built as drawn until the photography is commissioned.
risks: Notes become a blog nobody maintains
